_how_it_is_used: server_scripts/grindless/uxv/cas_a.js makes one recipe per entry, id grindless:<name> (GTM prefixes the type), with its programmed circuit; 'site' true locks the recipe to grindless:cas_a_remnant; 'kept' are not consumed; 'wear' is a kept input that a chance consumes (per ten thousand); an output with a 'chance' is a chanced output (count 1). The table has the two types of package UXV-B5 only; its older-table rows (calutron c14, cascade c22, hot cell c16-17, antimatter trap c5, profiler c3) live in their own tables and files, each marked UXV-B5.

recipes._why: machine 21 c1: the scoop sweeps Cassiopeia A's Ti-rich ejecta knots into dust. The matter is the remnant's (the row is locked to its dimension, the EMI page says so); one MH winding in fifty is worn out by the magnetic mouth. The dust is inert but for its titanium (EV extraction cascade c22); the rest is voided there.
recipes.name: sweep_ejecta_knots

recipes._why: machine 8 c1: a sealed Ti-44 core (worn out one run in fifty, the worn core goes to the IV hot cell, c17) feeds a solid-neon moderator cartridge; the positrons thermalise and bind as positronium, and the annihilation heat leaves in liquid helium, which warms to helium for the UEV He-3 polariser's cooling loop.
recipes.name: moderate_positronium

recipes._why: machine 8 c2: the UV antimatter trap's positron stack (c5) loads the moderated Ps cell, which condenses inside the gamma laser cavity; the MTJ die times the stimulated 511 keV pulse. The stack is annihilated in the pulse (line 25). The module leaves at the nose.
recipes.name: stimulate_gamma_emission
